text: Taking the native singular chain functor with coefficient object k gives the free left k-module on all continuous singular n-simplices in degree n. Its boundary is the alternating face sum and maps act by composition on simplices, matching [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=117). The published finite-support equivalence, pushforward formula and path-boundary equation verify these conventions directly. Arbitrary rings and empty spaces are allowed; this is the ordinary nonnegative chain complex. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L60).
Published coefficient identification on simplex generators.
Published pushforward on generators.
Published positive path boundary equals terminal minus initial point.

This is the canonical coproduct insertion of the coefficient a into the summand indexed by the singular simplex σ. Thus it represents aσ in the finite formal sums used by [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=117). The published coefficient equivalence sends it to `Finsupp.single σ a`, and scalar multiplication relates it to the unit-coefficient generator. It is a chain in degree n, with no requirement that σ be embedded, nondegenerate, or a cycle. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L68).
Published generator-to-singleton coefficient normalization.
Published aσ=a•(1σ).

Two k-linear maps out of the singular chain module agree once they agree on every simplex with coefficient one. Linearity then determines all coefficients and finite sums, exactly the universal property of the free chain module in [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=117). The proof uses the actual coproduct generator extensionality. No finite simplex set or commutative ring is required; for an empty space the domain is the zero module, so the conclusion remains correct. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L73).
Published relation recovering arbitrary coefficients from unit generators.

The chain map induced by f sends aσ to a(f∘σ). This preserves the coefficient and composes on the target side of the simplex, as in [Hatcher §2.1, induced chain maps](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=118). `TopCat.toSSet.map f` is the actual singular-simplex pushforward, and the proof uses its coproduct insertion equation. The statement holds in degree zero and for a=0; it requires neither injectivity of f nor any finiteness of X. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L88).
Published path specialization preserves composition with f.

A function assigning f(σ) in a k-module V to each singular simplex extends uniquely to a linear map on chains. The actual construction uses the coproduct universal property and sends aσ to a•f(σ), as its published evaluation theorem proves. This is the free-module interpretation of chains in [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=117). The assignment on simplices needs no continuity or finite support because each input chain itself has finite support. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L103).
Published evaluation on arbitrary coefficients.
Published exact values on unit generators.

The evaluation of the linear extension on aσ is a•f(σ), with a acting on the left in V. The proof reads the actual coproduct descent equation and evaluates the map k→V sending 1 to f(σ). It therefore matches the linear extension of finite formal sums in [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=117). In particular a=0 and a=1 give the expected values, without requiring commutativity of k or a finite set of simplices. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L109).
Published unit-coefficient specialization.

For coefficient one, the linear extension returns exactly the prescribed value f(σ). This is the unit-generator normalization of the free singular chain module from [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=117). The proof specializes the arbitrary-coefficient evaluation and uses `one_smul`, so it does not assume that V is an algebra or identify a scalar with a vector. The equation holds for every ring, left module and singular simplex, including degree zero. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L121).
Published full coefficient evaluation from which the normalization follows.

The equivalence identifies each singular chain with its finitely supported coefficient function on all singular n-simplices. Its inverse forms the corresponding finite linear combination; the two source proofs check both composites on generators. This realizes the finite formal sums defining chains in [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=117). The published forward and inverse singleton equations fix the correspondence, including zero coefficients. Neither finiteness of the simplex set nor commutativity of k is assumed. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L129).
Published forward singleton formula.
Published inverse singleton formula.

Under the coefficient equivalence, the chain aσ is exactly the finitely supported function with value a at σ and zero elsewhere. That pins the coefficient convention of the free singular chains in [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=117). The proof unfolds the chosen linear extension rather than introducing a new basis. Zero coefficients correctly produce the zero function, and repeated simplices combine by addition; no distinctness or nonzero-coefficient hypothesis is needed. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L139).
Published inverse equation checks the same normalization.

The definition linearly extends the constant assignment 1 on zero-simplices, so a finite chain is sent to the sum of its coefficients. This is exactly ε in [Hatcher §2.1, Proposition 2.7](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=118). Its published generator formula gives ε(aσ)=a, and naturality shows that moving points leaves the sum unchanged. The map exists for an empty space as well; the declaration asserts neither surjectivity nor a reduced-homology comparison without further hypotheses. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L172).
Published ε(aσ)=a.
Published naturality of augmentation.

The augmentation sends a zero-simplex with coefficient a to a itself. This is the coefficient-sum normalization of [Hatcher §2.1, Proposition 2.7](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=118), expressed for arbitrary ring coefficients. The proof evaluates the constant-one linear extension, giving a·1=a. No point of X is chosen globally: the supplied zero-simplex is the input. Consequently the theorem remains correctly quantified even for an empty X, and it makes no separate surjectivity assertion. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L177).
Published linear-extension formula used with constant value1.

Applying f to a zero-chain and then summing coefficients equals summing before pushforward. The map f may identify different points: their coefficients add, preserving the total. This is naturality of the augmentation from [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=118), and the source proves it by the actual generator pushforward and augmentation evaluations. Connectedness, injectivity and nonemptiness are correctly absent; the equality is for every zero-chain over an arbitrary ring. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L185).
Published coefficient-preserving pushforward.
Published augmentation on each generator.

The boundary of an (n+1)-simplex is the sum of its n+2 faces, with coefficient (−1)^i on the face omitting vertex i. The integer scalar acts on the chain module, so the formula works over any ring and retains the correct signs in characteristic 2. This matches [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=117). The published path specialization gives endpoint 1 minus endpoint 0, directly checking the low-degree orientation without constructing a new example. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L197).
Published degree1 boundary equals terminal point minus initial point.

Augmentation kills the boundary of every one-chain. On a singular edge the two zero-faces contribute a and −a, so their coefficient sum vanishes; linearity extends this to arbitrary finite chains. This is the ε∂₁=0 identity used in [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=118). The source uses the actual alternating boundary and augmentation formulas, with no connectedness or nonemptiness assumption. It asserts the chain condition, not the stronger equality kerε=im∂₁. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L209).
Published endpoint-difference formula confirms degree1 sign.
Published augmentation of each endpoint coefficient.

This chain map has target k concentrated in degree zero. Its zero component is the sum-of-coefficients augmentation, while every higher component lands in a zero module. The source supplies the chain condition ε∂₁=0, and its published zero-component equation fixes the map. This packages the augmentation of [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=118) as a map to the single complex. Contractibility or connectedness are needed for later exactness claims, not for defining this map. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L220).
Published coefficient-sum normalization in degree0.
Published chain condition ε∂₁=0.

The zero component of the augmentation chain map is `ModuleCat.ofHom` of the coefficient-sum linear map. This checks both the degree placement and the canonical augmentation normalization from [Hatcher §2.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=118). The proof uses the native map-to-single-complex equation, so no scalar factor or chosen point enters the comparison. It holds for all spaces and rings, including an empty space, and does not assert exactness or surjectivity. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/ModuleChains/Basic.lean#L228).
Published ε(aσ)=a verifies the component normalization.

This contravariant functor sends X to degreewise Hom(Xᵢ,Y), and a chain map to precomposition. Passing through opposite categories reverses the differential direction, giving a cochain complex rather than a chain complex. This is the Hom construction of [Hatcher §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=206). The published object and map equations identify it with Mathlib’s `linearYonedaObj` when C is abelian. The functor itself correctly requires only a preadditive k-linear category, not exactness of Hom. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/LinearYoneda.lean#L67).
Published identification with native linearYonedaObj in abelian case.
Published component precomposition formula.

A chain homotopy between φ and ψ becomes a cochain homotopy between φ* and ψ*, both directed from Hom(X′,Y) to Hom(X,Y). The published component formula sends a cochain g to g∘h, with indices reversed. This is exactly the dual-homotopy argument in [Hatcher §3.1, homotopy invariance](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=210). No additional sign is inserted: dualizing dh+hd exchanges the two summands. Preadditivity and k-linearity suffice; no projectivity or exactness assumption is needed. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/LinearYoneda.lean#L112).
Published component formula g↦h.hom j i ≫g.

The differential from cochain degree i to j sends g:Xᵢ→Y to g∘dⱼᵢ. Lean’s `X.d j i ≫ g` expresses exactly that composition. This is the coboundary convention of [Hatcher §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=206), with no extra sign or differential on Y because Y is a single coefficient object. The formula is stated for all index pairs: off the complex shape both sides vanish by the native differential convention. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/LinearYoneda.lean#L251).
Published coboundary formula has the same composition convention.

A cocycle of Hom(X,Y) annihilates the incoming boundaries of X: composing its underlying map with dⱼᵢ gives zero. The use of `iCycles` correctly extracts that underlying cochain, and the proof is the native kernel equation for cocycles. This matches the interpretation of cocycles in [Hatcher §3.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/AT/AT.pdf#page=206). It holds for every index pair, including off-shape zero differentials, without identifying cocycles with cohomology classes or assuming that all cocycles are coboundaries. [Source](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/LinearYoneda.lean#L256).
Published differential-as-precomposition identifies the zero composite.

The conclusion is eventual uniform smallness of the moment tails on d(x,y)≥R, exactly the moment condition in [Villani’s draft, Definition 6.6/Theorem 6.7](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=84). Finite positive p makes d(x,·)^p a continuous nonnegative function, and finiteness of the limiting moment prevents mass from escaping with nonvanishing cost. The radius may depend on ε but not on the eventual index. The published [reverse tail criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Moment.lean#L144) controls d(x,y)>R, with a larger radius reconciling the boundaries. Arbitrary filters are allowed; this does not assert control of every early term.
Published converse tail-to-moment convergence criterion, with its explicit open-tail convention.

The integrand is d(x,y)^q on the open set d(x,y)>r and zero elsewhere. Its strict superlevel sets are open, so the weak integral is lower semicontinuous by the [published nonnegative-integral principle](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/Measure/LowerSemicontinuousLintegral.lean#L85). The strict boundary is essential. Any real q is valid in ENNReal: negative powers have the extended value at zero, but zero-distance points lie outside this open tail. The theorem claims lower semicontinuity, without finiteness or continuity of the tail integral.
Published weak lower-semicontinuity principle for nonnegative lower-semicontinuous integrands.

Inside the closed radius-r ball, d(x,y)^q≤r^q because q≥0; outside, the displayed tail integral retains the integrand. Integrating this pointwise bound gives exactly r^q plus the open-tail contribution, since ν has mass 1. The [published moment-convergence criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Moment.lean#L144) uses the same open-tail convention. Zero radius and q=0 satisfy the literal ENNReal formula; no finite-moment assumption is needed for an inequality with possible infinite values.

Weak convergence plus the stated eventual tail bound gives convergence of the q-moments, as in [Villani’s draft, Definition 6.6/Theorem 6.7](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=84). For q>0, thresholding d(x,·)^q is equivalent to thresholding distance; using r+1 converts the open spatial tail into the closed superlevel set needed by the integral criterion. The published [converse criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Moment.lean#L82) controls the other direction when the limiting moment is finite. The conclusion is ENNReal convergence along the given filter, without an assertion about all initial terms.
Published finite-limit moment convergence gives eventual uniformly small radial tails.

The radial Lp norm equals Wp(δx,μ) by the [published Dirac identity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L454). The triangle inequality therefore bounds its change by Wp(μ,ν), proving the claimed continuity. At p=∞ the functional is an essential distance bound, not an integral raised to 1/∞; the [actual Lp convention](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Defs.lean#L92) covers this endpoint. The installed Wasserstein topology requires p≥1 and the stated Borel/standard-Borel assumptions. No finite-p weak-convergence characterization is extended to ∞.
Actual distance from a Dirac law equals the radial Lp seminorm, including∞.

For 1≤p<∞, the displayed integral is the p-th power of the radial Lp norm. The [published norm-continuity result](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Moment.lean#L170) and continuity of nonnegative real powers give precisely its continuity. This is the necessity half of [Villani’s draft, Definition 6.6/Theorem 6.7](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=84). The explicit p≠∞ condition prevents the exponent `p.toReal` from replacing the infinity endpoint by zero. The supporting [integrability theorem](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Moment.lean#L204) confirms that the corresponding real moment is genuine on this carrier.
Published continuity of the radial Lp norm in the actual Wp topology.
Actual finite-p real moment is integrable for members of the finite-moment carrier.

Wasserstein convergence supplies weak convergence and convergence of the finite p-moment. Applying the [published tail criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Moment.lean#L82) yields exactly the eventual bound on d(x,y)≥R. This matches [Villani’s draft, Definition 6.6/Theorem 6.7](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=84)’s moment-tail condition. The finite exponent restriction is essential and explicit; the source does not infer this characterization at ∞. The bound is uniform only on an eventual set of indices, as both Lean and the docstring state.
Published finite-limit moment convergence gives eventual uniformly small radial tails.
Published finite-p moment continuity supplies convergence of the same displayed integral.

This is the sufficient direction of [Villani’s draft, Definition 6.6/Theorem 6.7](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=84): weak convergence plus convergence of radial p-moments to a finite limit forces Wp→0. The native proof separates a bounded transport cost from two moment tails, so it remains valid for 0<p<1 without invoking a metric triangle inequality. The [published tail criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Moment.lean#L82) supplies those tails. Separability and measurable opens are explicit; completeness, optimal-plan attainment and finite moments at every early index are unnecessary.
Published finite-limit moment convergence gives eventual uniformly small radial tails.
Published Pp specialization of the raw weak-plus-moment convergence implication.

The right side states weak convergence of the same probability laws and convergence of their p-moments about the specified point. The two native directions—[weak continuity](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/WeakConvergence.lean#L143) and [moment sufficiency](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Moment.lean#L254)—identify this with convergence in the installed Wp topology. This matches [Villani’s draft, Definition 6.6/Theorem 6.7](https://www.ceremade.dauphine.fr/~mischler/articles/VBook-O%26N.pdf#page=84). Both 1≤p and p<∞ are retained. Pseudometric bases and arbitrary filters introduce no point-separation claim, and no completeness hypothesis is needed merely to characterize convergence.
Published forgetful inclusion is continuous to the actual weak probability topology.
Published sufficiency from weak convergence plus finite limiting radial moment.

The pushforward change-of-variables formula identifies radial Lp integrability under f#μ with Lp integrability of x↦d(f(x),z) under μ. The [published basepoint criterion](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Basic.lean#L696) makes this equivalent to the actual finite-moment predicate. Finiteness of μ and an ordinary pseudometric target permit any specified z; a.e. measurability of f is enough. At∞ this is essential boundedness, while p=0 retains the precise [MemLp convention](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Defs.lean#L92). No topology on the source is required.
Published finite-measure basepoint criterion on an ordinary pseudometric target.

Push the supplied coupling forward by (f,f). Its displacement is at most K times the original displacement, so its Lp objective bounds the new Wasserstein infimum. The [published pushforward-plan bound](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Pushforward.lean#L109) fixes this comparison. A specified coupling makes K=0 legitimate even when its original cost is infinite: the image displacement is zero. Target distance measurability is explicit, and the [Lp definition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/MeasureTheory/Function/LpSeminorm/Defs.lean#L92) supports both p=0 and∞.
Actual mapped source coupling bounds transport between the two image laws.

Taking infima of the [published coupling estimate](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Pushforward.lean#L177) yields the stated K-Lipschitz bound. The nonzero condition matters for arbitrary measures: if no source coupling exists, its distance is∞ and K·∞ remains∞. Thus unequal masses and infinite costs are included honestly. No optimal coupling is assumed; the strict-infimum characterization suffices. The formula uses finite NNReal K and every Lp exponent, including∞, without imposing probability normalization.
Published estimate for a specified coupling, including zero Lipschitz constant.
No coupling gives actual extended distance∞; this checks the arbitrary-measure empty-infimum case.

The supplied existence of a source coupling permits K=0: its image is a zero-displacement coupling, giving distance 0. For K>0 the [published arbitrary-measure estimate](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Pushforward.lean#L201) applies. This is exactly the extra hypothesis needed because ENNReal has 0·∞=0; without a coupling, unequal masses would retain infinite distance after pushforward. The statement preserves this distinction and makes no finite-cost or optimizer assumption.
Published arbitrary-measure estimate with the necessary positive Lipschitz factor.
Published estimate for a specified coupling, including zero Lipschitz constant.

For probability laws the independent product is a coupling, so the [general coupling-existence estimate](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Pushforward.lean#L223) gives the asserted K-Lipschitz pushforward bound, including K=0. The native [translation invariance](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Convolution.lean#L104) and [translation displacement bound](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/d96e9ceca01f4548b817649c5ae95e33c6fc3ae4/TauCeti/MeasureTheory/OptimalTransport/Wasserstein/Convolution.lean#L128) pass the applicable roadmap controls. The target’s distance measurability is explicit. At p=∞ this compares essential-supremum costs; p=0 follows the stated seminorm convention, without claiming a metric there.
Native common-translation isometry equality, directly exercising the reviewed map_eq theorem.
Roadmap translation bound: any probability law and its translate differ by Wp at most the translating norm.
Roadmap canonical equality: real seminormed-space law and its translate are exactly the translating norm apart for1≤p.

A witness x for the source moment yields the target witness f(x). The radial bound d(f(x),f(y))≤K d(x,y) transfers MemLp after pushforward change of variables.
